Subject: Equinox model – elevated 5xx/timeouts and recovery update

Hi Alicia / Skyline team,

I wanted to let you know we observed an elevated error/timeout rate impacting the Equinox (equinox-13b) model serving in your us-west region starting ~08:55 PDT this morning. Symptoms: an increase in 5xx errors and timeouts for generation requests, particularly for long-context (>2k tokens). Our initial automated routing shifted some traffic to a smaller fallback model but we know you pin to Equinox for quality — we wanted to be transparent.

What we know so far:
- Start: ~2029-03-15 08:55 PDT.
- Impact: 10–18% of requests receive 500/504s or end in server-side timeout (seen mainly on batch jobs and high-token streams).
- Scope: ~3% of your overall requests; spikes concentrated on two nodes in the us-west pool.

Immediate actions were taking:
1) Ops: isolating the two affected GPU workers and routing traffic away from them.
2) Runtime team: disabling a speculative kernel optimization introduced in last weeks release and rolling that change back on affected hosts.
3) Mitigation: automatic retrier is enabled for idempotent requests and were applying temporary request-size guards for streaming sessions.

Were attaching the initial error logs and SLO snapshot; more detailed root cause analysis and a postmortem draft will follow.

Short ask: Can you confirm whether any production jobs pinned to equinox-13b are running long-context batched jobs this morning? That will help us prioritize routed capacity.

Im available on this thread and for a quick call if you prefer (15–30m).

Thanks and sorry for the disruption — well keep you updated as we have concrete fixes.

--

Quick internal update and proposed customer note: 

Summary of triage so far:
- Root cause hypothesis: a kernel selection path added to accelerate long-sequence attention is causing memory fragmentation on older Ampere instances under certain batching patterns. This leads to intermittent OOM-like errors surfaced as 5xx at the service layer.
- Evidence: logs show repeated "kv_cache_alloc_failed" traces on two worker hosts (ip ends .42 and .57) that correlate with high-request token counts.

Mitigation already applied:
- Isolated hosts .42/.57 and rerouted traffic; autoscaler brought up healthy replacements within ~7 minutes.
- Rolled back the kernel path on the affected hosts and disabled the optimization globally as a precaution.
- Temporarily lowered max_stream_token_size from 4096 -> 2048 for streaming sessions in us-west to reduce memory pressure.

Impact assessment for Skyline:
- Expected functional delta: short-term reduction in maximum stream length for streaming sessions; summarization outputs for prompts >2k tokens may be split across calls or truncated if clients don't handle continuation tokens. We estimate ~2–3% reduction in fidelity for those specific long-run cases.

Suggested customer communication (draft):
- Confirmed root cause hypothesis and that rollback plus host isolation has stabilized error rates.
- Suggest pause of non-critical long-context batch runs for 2–4 hours.
- Offer 25% pro-rated credit for compute time during the incident window (negotiable).
- Deliverables: full postmortem within 48 hours, cleaned logs, and a remediation timeline for the kernel fix plus tests.

Requesting: Rachel, can you send the above and confirm whether Skyline accepts the credit offer or wants an alternative make-good? Also looping Neha for SLA/comp approval.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
